tour.title: Workshop Site Overview
tour.description: Begin at the represented event listing to understand this Next.js site: visitors discover workshops, register for events, and access learning resources. Its event cards introduce the dates, delivery format, and pricing that the next steps trace into shared data and registration.

tour.title: Event Data And Routes
tour.description: Follow the listing into the shared event catalogue, a widely referenced foundation for event pages and checkout. The dynamic detail route resolves a slug and promotional code before rendering the event view. Status helpers distinguish ended events, manual closure, and scheduled registration cutoffs so those states can receive different presentation.

tour.title: Registration And Payment
tour.description: Building on the catalogue, the registration component collects attendee details and handles donations, promo codes, free reservations, and embedded or hosted Stripe checkout. The checkout library constructs branded payment parameters and carries reservation expiry and attribution metadata. Read the accompanying tests to see the intended pricing, return-flow, and closure boundaries.

tour.title: Festival Presentation
tour.description: The same event data also drives a specialized Joechella presentation. Its hero introduces the event, the timeline groups programming and access notes, and the venue gallery combines imagery with optional video. These components show how an event-specific experience fits inside the shared landing-page architecture.

tour.title: Attendee Learning Resources
tour.description: After registration, event setup pages give attendees preparation instructions and next steps. The session guide expands that learning journey into browser workflows, local transcription, package scanning, and Git checkpoints. The lead magnet workshop guide provides another example of detailed instructional content delivered through the site.

tour.title: Shared Giveaway Rendering
tour.description: Giveaways form the second major visitor journey alongside workshops. The heavily reused PackPage component renders structured content, copyable commands, personalized prompts, matched offers, and email capture. Its content model and tool adapter separate interactive presentation from resource-specific instructions and generated HowTo metadata.

tour.title: Catalog Backed Tool Guides
tour.description: With that rendering contract established, explore the Free AI Tools catalogue and routes that select a tool from it. The Compositor, Open Design, and Claude Video Skills pages illustrate reusable setup guides and structured search metadata. The catalogue tests protect route coverage, prerequisites, delivery links, and audience targeting as this family expands.

tour.title: Curated Guides And Prompts
tour.description: Some resources need dedicated content rather than a standard catalogue entry. GuardDog shares a pinned setup prompt between its guide and delivery email, while the five free tool swaps pack explains alternatives, limits, and follow-on offers. The film resource pairs guide content with a reusable prompt, showing the same separation of presentation and instructions.

tour.title: Lead Capture And Delivery
tour.description: Once a visitor requests a guide, the lead-magnet API validates the source, checks suppression, records lead information, and dispatches the appropriate email. Catalogue-driven email builders keep setup instructions aligned with the website, while generic delivery code restricts destinations to approved mappings. The lazy Supabase client supports data access without requiring production configuration at import time.

tour.title: Discovery Metadata And Offers
tour.description: The resources just delivered also need consistent discovery and next-step links. The giveaway registry and sitemap describe available resources, while route layouts provide canonical and social metadata. Shared offer definitions select the relevant continuation and add campaign parameters to its destination.

tour.title: Guarded Follow Up Workflows
tour.description: Resource delivery continues into follow-up planning, where shared rules determine copy, timing, audience eligibility, suppression, and human handoff. A separate operational runner coordinates previews and claimed sends using external account checks. Read the tests and unsubscribe handler alongside it to understand the eligibility and opt-out boundaries around those actions.

tour.title: Desk Pet Distribution Contract
tour.description: Return to a concrete delivered resource to see why source text and published assets must stay aligned. The Desk Pet pack and canonical prompt describe setup, personalization, installation, and removal, while the downloadable prompt is the instruction document recipients actually receive. Tests check prompt parity and packaged assets, connecting the content model to its distribution contract.

tour.title: Download Integrity And Coverage
tour.description: The LinkedIn Kit provides a parallel example for archive-based delivery. Its pack and prompt supply the resource content, while the public ZIP and SHA-256 file represent the distributed archive and its integrity check. The associated test checks the page and registered content, illustrating a separate concern from whether an archive is intact.

tour.title: Routing And Legacy Delivery
tour.description: Finish with the configuration that determines which of those resource URLs reaches users. Next.js configuration controls tracing, media exclusions, host rewrites, and legacy redirects, including the former free Video Editor page and archive now pointing to the paid Video Agent. Comparing the legacy page and its source tests makes clear why asset presence alone does not prove the destination served by a redirected URL.

project.name: masterminds-workshop
